name: Siculo Arabic
notes:
Siculo Arabic (sqr), the Arabic of Sicily, Malta and Pantelleria from roughly the 9th to the 13th century, and the ancestor of Maltese. ATTESTED, NOT DESCRIBED HERE. The ISO 639-3 registry lists it as an extinct individual language within the Arabic macrolanguage; no phonological description has been read into this spec, and the grapheme table is inherited from ar-x-maghrebi and is a placeholder rather than a claim — no reflex below has been checked against a source.

THE PARENT IS A GROUPING, NOT A DESCRIPTION. Siculo Arabic is conventionally placed with the Maghrebi group on historical grounds, so the Maghrebi proto-node is the honest parent: it asserts the grouping the literature asserts and nothing finer. Parenting it to a modern national variety would claim a descent no source supports, and parenting it to Maltese would invert the direction of descent.

An extinct variety is written from manuscript evidence rather than from speakers, so a description here would rest on orthographic reconstruction; that is a different evidence bar from a living dialect and should be stated when one is written.
